h1: The 8 Best Electric Kettles Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Electric Kettles Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best electric kettles under $200, from glass gooseneck models to 1500W stainless steel, compared on size and material.
summary: The Chefman with Temperature Control and gooseneck spout is our top pick for tea and pour-over fans. The Cuisinart is the 1500W stainless-feel option at the top of the price range, and the Amazon Basics stainless kettle gives 1.7L and 1500W for under $25. The Hamilton Beach 1L is the lowest-cost compact choice.
intro: A budget of $200 is far more than a kettle needs, and the spec sheets prove it: several kettles in this list cost under $25 and match the wattage of the priciest. What the extra money actually buys is control, specifically temperature settings and a gooseneck spout.
We reviewed eight kettles on paper, comparing capacity, wattage, material, and any temperature or spout features. Because the ceiling is generous, the ranking rewards features over raw price.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle with Temperature Control
products.verdict: A glass gooseneck kettle with temperature control.
products.description:
This Chefman kettle pairs a glass body with 1.8L capacity and a gooseneck spout, plus the temperature control named in the title. It sits at $25 to $50.

The spout and temperature control are what push it past the plain 1500W kettles below, because they let you pour slowly for coffee and stop below boiling for green tea. The wattage is not listed in the data we have.

Buy it if you brew tea or pour-over coffee. The caveat is the missing wattage figure.
products.idealFor: Tea drinkers and pour-over coffee fans.
products.skipIf: You only boil water for instant meals.

products.name: Cuisinart Electric Kettle
products.verdict: 1500W and 1.7L from a major appliance brand.
products.description:
The Cuisinart lists 1500W and a 1.7L capacity, and it is the only pick in the $100 to $200 bracket. That makes it the one that uses the top of this budget.

It is second because the spec sheet shows no temperature setting or special spout, so you are paying for brand and capacity rather than new functions. The plain 1500W kettles below match its numbers for far less.

Choose it if you value the Cuisinart name. The caveat is price against equal specs.
cons: Costs far more than equal specs
products.skipIf: You want the best value for the money.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Stainless Steel Kettle for Tea and Coffee
products.description:
Amazon Basics offers a stainless steel body with 1500W and 1.7L capacity, and it is priced under $25. That is the same wattage and volume as the Cuisinart at a fraction of the cost.

It trails the Chefman because it lacks temperature control or a gooseneck, but if you just want fast boiling it is hard to beat on value.

Buy it for plain, quick boiling. The caveat is that there are no special controls.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants quick boiling on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You brew tea at specific temperatures.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle
products.description:
The plain Chefman combines a glass body, 1500W, and a 1.8L capacity, at under $25. It is the largest kettle in the group by volume.

It sits below the Chefman with Temperature Control because it lacks the temperature settings and gooseneck, though it lists a confirmed 1500W that the control model does not.

Choose it if you boil for several people and like seeing the water. The caveat is that it has no extras.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A plastic 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
Cosori sells a plastic 1.7L kettle at $25 to $50, and the data we have lists no wattage.

With the Amazon Basics steel kettle offering confirmed 1500W for less, the Cosori has to win on brand or looks. Plastic is light but the least premium material here.

Buy it for a light, simple kettle. The caveat is the missing power figure.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a light kettle.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Kettle with Glass Carafe for Tea and Coffee
products.verdict: A 1L glass kettle with 1500W for tight counters.
products.description:
This Amazon Basics glass carafe kettle holds 1L and draws 1500W, at under $25. It is the compact glass option.

Only 1L means more refills than the 1.7L kettles, but the small body saves counter space.

Buy it for a single person or a small kitchen. The caveat is capacity.

products.name: OVENTE 1.7L Electric Kettle with 1100W Fast Boiling Water
products.description:
OVENTE offers a stainless steel body, 1.7L capacity, and 1100W of power, at under $25.

The 1100W is 400W below the 1500W kettles, so it boils slower for the same volume. Amazon Basics steel is the better buy at the same price.

Buy it only if you find it at a discount or prefer the look. The caveat is the lower wattage.
products.idealFor: Buyers who don't mind waiting a bit longer.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A 1L tea kettle at the lowest price, with few specs listed.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach sells a 1 liter tea kettle at under $25. The only spec in the data is the capacity, with no wattage or material.

That thin sheet is why it finishes last: you cannot compare its boil speed with the others.

Buy it if you want a name-brand small kettle at the lowest price. The caveat is that you should verify the specs.
products.idealFor: One-person kitchens on a minimal budget.
products.skipIf: You want to compare power and material.

whatMatters.detail: Different teas need different water temperatures; green tea is typically brewed below boiling. A kettle with temperature settings lets you stop at the right point. Check the title or bullets for 'temperature control'.
A gooseneck has a long, thin spout that gives a slow, steady pour, which is needed for pour-over coffee. Standard spouts pour faster and less precisely. Look for 'gooseneck' in the listing.
Wattage sets boil speed, with 1500W faster than 1100W. Some listings omit it. Look for the number in the specs.
Liters decide how many cups you boil at once. 1L suits one person, 1.7L to 1.8L suits a household. Compare the listed liters to your usual use.
Glass shows water level, steel is tougher, and plastic is lightest. The material affects handling. Read the material in the title or bullets.

faq.q: Do I need to spend near $200 on a kettle?
faq.a: No. Several kettles here cost under $25 and list 1500W. The extra money mostly buys brand or control features.
Paying for the Cuisinart's price when equal wattage exists for less.
If you brew green tea or pour-over coffee, yes. For plain boiling, no.

finalTake: The Chefman with Temperature Control is the best kettle here if you brew tea or pour-over coffee. For plain boiling, the Amazon Basics steel kettle matches the Cuisinart's 1500W for far less. Decide whether you need control features first, and the price choice is easy.
